title: Python: a del statement binds a name in Python but the walker records none; ALIAS-adjacent gaps shared with m.attr() and C.m() (follow-up from the GCLI-113 review)
description: Found in the GCLI-113 round 1 review. (1) The walker has no delete_statement arm: `del f` makes f local to its function in Python (so a nested `nonlocal f` is legal and a read of f is a local read), but no binding is recorded. Today the effect is that applyScopeRedirects falls back to the nearest enclosing function and a binding written by a nonlocal in a nested scope can be the only recorded binding of the local; ALIAS reads B at the binding's origin to stay correct. A del of the NAME is also not counted by enumerableBindings for 6d, R4, K1, LIT, M1 and ALIAS (e.g. `x = C(); del x; x = D()`-style sequences are unaffected because the other bindings are counted, but a name whose only binding is deleted and re-bound by a nonlocal write is not seen). Fix in the walker (record a del target as a binding kind that refuses every rule), with a refused fixture per rule, and a five-pin corpus diff that names any site that moves. (2) Gaps ALIAS shares with the direct m.attr() and C.m() resolution and does not widen, named for the same task: a package __init__ def shadowed by a submodule of the same name, Cls.attr = v or setattr(Cls, ...) from outside the module, metaclass descriptors, a decorated class, an opaque base before an in-repo def, rule 44 (type = m.func). Not in the DEC-303 build order; a follow-up. DEC-303 (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a del of a local or a module-level name is recorded as a binding that makes 6d, R4, K1, LIT, M1 and ALIAS refuse the name, with a refused fixture per rule asserting no edge leaves the call site and the bin is unchanged, and a positive twin
the shared gaps named in the description each get a fixture recording today behaviour (resolves or refuses) and a decision for the operator route if a fix is wanted
a per-site five-pin corpus diff is recorded and any site that moves is named
